highlights.title: Regular Tech Bros Are Worried About Honeypots
highlights.summary: The Jensen Huang scandal is the latest fuel for dating anxieties among newly rich and powerful tech workers.
body: When the founder of a cybersecurity firm hired Blaine Anderson as a matchmaker, it wasn’t just because the man was lonely. It was also, Anderson says, because he was “super worried about spies.”

The cybersecurity founder isn’t the only one. As Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security dominates headlines and AI companies reportedly warn employees against “honeypots,” matchmakers say that more men with pretty normal lives are worried that their dates may have ulterior motives: accessing corporate secrets.
“Even if you're not a CEO or at a big tech giant, these fears have trickled down to just regular professionals,” Simone Grossman, a Brooklyn-based matchmaker, tells WIRED.
One tech worker, who requested anonymity in order to speak candidly, says he considers himself “highly selective” about the people he interacts with face-to-face.

highlights.summary: ATP Finals updates from the afternoon action in Turin Mail Katy | Kartal’s fightback against injury and abuse. And talking about Agassi: this is a lovely trip down memory lane of the 1990 season-ending final. Buongiorno!
body: Buongiorno! With Carlos Alcaraz already guaranteed to finish top of the Ivan Lendl group after two straight-sets wins, the biggest jeopardy going into his match against the already-eliminated Flavio Cobolli is the state of his left hamstring. After picking up the injury against Daniil Medvedev on Wednesday, Alcaraz had an MRI scan yesterday and was cleared to play on, so now we’ll get to see if he can still hit the absurd levels he did earlier this week.

While Alcaraz is riding a late-season wave after his wrist injury-enforced summer hiatus, sweeping up titles in Tokyo, Vienna and Paris, Cobolli was reduced to tears after the 7-6, 6-0 loss to Frances Tiafoe that sealed his exit two days ago. The Italian – the only home player in the Jannik Sinner-less singles – said it was the saddest match of his career and that he felt he’d let the Turin crowd down on his ATP Finals debut. But Cobolli still described today’s meeting with Alcaraz – just the second of his career – as “a beautiful gift … I hope to annoy him as much as possible, even if it won’t be easy”.

highlights.title: Total War: Warhammer 40,000 breaks the game into star system mini-campaigns, each with their own stories and objectives
highlights.summary: There is perhaps nothing so brutal in a Total War game than getting an army full of elite units wiped out, and it appears that pain remains a factor in the upcoming Total War conversion of: Warhammer 40,000.
body: In an hour-long deep-dive livestream of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, developer Creative Assembly demonstrated the game in action, focusing initially on how armies navigate from planet to planet. Each star system apparently acts as a "contained campaign" you can hop between in the game.

The star system the stream focused on is Praevoss, a mid-sized collection of planets: three of which you can land on and fight on, while the others are smaller and unable to support your tactical warfare shenanigans. Once you're finished with a star system, you move on, carrying over units and unlocked skills.

"First and foremost, we want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy, which is just not possible on a single Total War map," Creative Assembly explained on the livestream. "You'd never be able to engage with it. Part of the point is to break this up a bit and allow us to have some more interesting and more bespoke narratives going on. So each of these star systems has a premise, has a narrative, has a specific setup, a specific start, [and] specific victory objectives that you've got to go and do."

highlights.title: Candle Media’s Kevin Mayer Says ‘Urge to Merge’ Will Last Several Years as Revenue Growth Stalls
highlights.summary: If there is one thing Candle Media founder Kevin Mayer understands, it is mergers. The exec oversaw Disney’s 2019 acquisition of 21st Century Fox during his term as the company’s chief strategy officer, where he was also involved in Disney’s acquisition of Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm and BAMTech.
body: “You see NBCUniversal not only being split off of Comcast but itself being split between cable networks and the rest of the studio and the rest of the streaming business,” he added. “Those splits are intended to ultimately lead to consolidation of those two companies with other companies. So you are seeing this urge to merge driven by basic financial dynamics, and that is: when growth slows, you want to take that revenue base and amortize it over a smaller cost base.” This movement, Mayer added, will be an “ongoing process for the next several years.”

Still weighing in on Hollywood’s merger fever, Mayer looked back at his own experience at Disney, noting how “easy” it is to “mess up an acquisition.” Bringing two companies together is a process that needs to be done “very carefully,” he said, recalling when Disney bought Pixar from under the realm of former CEO Steve Jobs in 2006.

“Jobs was a very loud voice on this one,” he noted, going on to tell the audience how, from his very first meeting with the Apple founder, former Disney CEO Bob Iger went straight into ironing out how to avoid the possible “cultural issues” of the merger.

highlights.title: Why the robots are ditching Uber
highlights.summary: In a late August earnings call, Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi sounded optimistic about his company's "very strong" partnership with Waymo, the global leader in autonomous robotaxis.
body: Waymo and Serve Robotics are walking away from exclusive deals. Can Uber still be the default app for autonomy?
“We believe we’ll continue to operate next year in those marketplaces,” he gushed. “It’s a terrific product, and the on-the-ground partnership continues to be very strong.”

The partnership would turn out to be more brittle than Khosrowshahi let on. Several weeks later, Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana revealed in an interview that her company planned to end its exclusive robotaxi partnership with Uber, calling the mixed-fleet experience a “crapshoot” for its own customers. Starting in January 2028, riders in Austin and Atlanta will be able to use the Waymo app to hail driverless rides directly. The unlikely partnership, it would seem, was coming to an end.

Waymo isn’t alone in souring on its experience in the Uber ecosystem. Serve Robotics, which operates thousands of sidewalk delivery robots in dozens of US cities, recently announced it would not renew its partnership with Uber Eats when it expires in 2027.

highlights.title: This 16-Year-Old Founded an AI Missile Startup. He’s Targeting ‘Cost per Kill’
highlights.summary: Henrijs Dandzbergs dropped out of high school to join startup accelerator Y Combinator. With a new breed of missile, he wants to make killing as efficient as possible for the US and its military allies.
body: At 16 years old, Henrijs Dandzbergs is too young to vote. Or drink. Or smoke. Or drive unsupervised. But he’s not too young to win half a million dollars for his AI-guided- missile startup.

In September, Dandzbergs, who was born in Latvia, was admitted to Y Combinator’s fall 2026 cohort. The startup accelerator counts companies like Airbnb, Stripe, DoorDash, and Reddit among its alumni; Dandzbergs is likely the youngest solo founder in its vaunted history.

His startup, Polemos Industries, is attempting to develop a new class of precision-guided missile that can be easily and cheaply manufactured, can be fired from portable launchers, and can resist jamming attempts. “I think missiles are the coolest thing,” Dandzbergs tells WIRED. “A lot of people that have found success in engineering early on have had a passion for blowing stuff up.”

In conversation, Dandzbergs is poised and articulate. He talks about “attacking hard problems,” breaking things down to “first principles,” and how the Ukraine conflict has forever altered the theater of war—a personal fixation, given his country's proximity to Russia. He projects an unassailable confidence in his own abilities.

highlights.title: AI helps researchers investigate how thousands of medical studies share code
highlights.summary: An MIT and Dana-Farber Institute-led team used large language models to examine nearly 4,000 studies and hundreds of code repositories, revealing gaps in the information needed to scrutinize and reuse published research.
body: The data and code that underpin a research study can tell us what was actually done, and how. In a medical study, for example, how were patients selected for inclusion? How were missing values handled? How were the results evaluated?
Access to a study's data and code help researchers to answer these questions, to examine the methods, and to build on the work.

“Studies involve many choices about how to prepare data, develop models, and evaluate performance. These are sometimes called ‘researcher degrees of freedom,’” says Tom Pollard, a research scientist at MIT's Laboratory for Computational Physiology and Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory. “The choices we make affect the results, and a methods section in a paper can only capture so much detail.”

While sharing code can be a first step, in order for code to be understood and reused, it must be sufficiently structured and described. The problem is that, right now, there is little guidance for researchers on what constitutes a well-organized, well-described collection of code.

highlights.summary: Scotland are forced into a late change for Saturday's Nations Championship visit by Japan after Rory Darge, who was due to captain the side, is ruled out through injury.
body: Scotland have been forced into a late change for Saturday's Nations Championship visit of Japan after Rory Darge, who was due to captain the side, was ruled out through injury.

The Glasgow Warriors forward had been carrying a shoulder injury from last weekend's win over Australia and, following further assessment and discussion within the Scotland camp, it has been decided he will sit out the game at Murrayfield.

Club-mate Matt Fagerson will start instead at number eight, with his place on the bench filled by Edinburgh flanker Freddy Douglas and Newcastle Red Bulls' Ollie Leatherbarrow moving forward in the back row.
Head coach Gregor Townsend had already made 10 changes for Japan's visit with several top players, including fly-half Finn Russell, rested.

Should the results be accurate, it'll dramatically eclipse GTA 6's $1bn in three days result. It'll also put GTA 6 on track to reach the eye-watering $3.25bn to $5.2bn week-one sales estimates for GTA 6.

So far, Rockstar has said nothing in relation to GTA 6's sales since the game was released around the world yesterday. Parent company Take-Two has said the game's pre-orders were tracking "well above expectations, and GTA 6 broke pre-order records on both the PlayStation Store and the Xbox Store, though, so all signs point to a record-breaking release. The question is "by how much?".

Reaction to GTA 6 has been glittering. Chris awarded GTA 6 five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, calling it "a game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale". "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that."

highlights.title: Muse Is Unleashing a World of Pettiness on Instagram
highlights.summary: Meta’s AI assistant can track and unfollow Instagram users who don’t follow you back—and some people are taking full advantage.
body: Khalil Roberts had heard horror stories of people getting kicked off Instagram for using third-party apps to purge follower counts, so when he came across an X post claiming that Muse — Meta ’s AI assistant —could mass-unfollow people who didn’t follow him back, he didn’t believe it.

“I’ve never gone through my exact list to vet those people out, but I’ve always been curious,” the 31-year-old New Yorker tells WIRED. But after realizing that by using Muse, his account wouldn’t get flagged as spam, his mind was made up. “I was like, I actually will be a little petty.”

Within minutes, Muse identified 151 accounts. It attached an Excel sheet with a breakdown of everyone cataloged—separated by categories identifying their username, real name, classification, and profile link—and asked if Roberts wanted to proceed with his request. Shockingly, some of the names were people he thought of as friends. “It was a little surprising, but also a reminder that we don’t have a relationship anymore.”
points: Meta’s AI assistant can track and unfollow Instagram users who don’t follow you back—and some people are taking full advantage.

body: That is a "tale of two cities" that did not look too likely to get written when Mark Robins' Potters started this season with three straight defeats and Blues won only two of their first eight league games under Chris Davies.
But, just like you should never judge a book by its cover, the footballing equivalent is to never judge any league table until after 10 games.
The season is now three months old - after Saturday's meeting at the Bet365 Stadium it will be more than a third of the way in.
And a clearer picture is starting to emerge as to whether what was once the "worst of times", especially in Stoke's case, might yet become the "best of times" before this 46-game campaign ends.

highlights.title: Every Future Driving Game Needs to Steal This GTA 6 Feature
highlights.summary: I've written numerous times about my love for open-world driving games. I love racing, but I also love cruising, taking in the landscape, setting out on road trips. My heart belongs to Test Drive Unlimited. I've written a tourist guide for the Forza Horizon series.
body: Grand Theft Auto 6 has instantly joined my driving-game canon thanks to one tiny, but revolutionary, feature.

On the PlayStation 5 version of GTA 6, Rockstar Games has come up with a genius application for the DualSense controller's adaptive triggers. When driving, the right trigger (the throttle) provides gentle resistance when cruising at the speed limit. The effect is a sort of soft stop for the trigger; your finger rests easily there, but it's also easy to push past it when you want to put your foot down.

I cannot overstate how much I love this. If you want to cruise, you no longer need to hover your finger in an approximate spot, making tiny adjustments to try to match speed with the traffic. You can just rest it against the soft stop, the way you just rest your foot on the accelerator pedal in a real car. It's so chill.

highlights.title: The 22 Best European Christmas Markets to Visit This Winter
highlights.summary: From Vienna to Helsinki, there’s nothing quite like a Christmas market to offer a mood-boosting hit of festive splendor. Here, find 22 immersive European Christmas markets to make this your merriest holiday season yet.
body: There’s nothing quite like a Christmas market to set a joyful tone for the holiday season. Is there anywhere else where it’s acceptable to mill about with a hearty mug of glögg in one hand, an even larger potato pancake in the other, while exceeding your budget on handcrafted ornaments and posing for photos in front of a wooden sleigh? The answer, we can confidently say, is no.

If you’re especially fortunate, you might even find yourself exploring a traditional European Christmas market this winter—a bucket list item for travelers with a proclivity for all things merry and bright. A natural place to start when curating an itinerary is Germany, and for good reason: It is, after all, the birthplace of the Christmas market, with Dresden’s Striezelmarkt first springing up all the way back in 1434.

But it’s hardly the only country that excels at this holiday event. There are numerous other destinations scattered across the continent—some familiar, and some wonderfully under the radar—that deliver the festive goods. Here, find 22 storybook European Christmas markets to make 2026 your most memorable holiday season yet.

highlights.title: The Smart Ring Goes to Church
highlights.summary: From glowing crosses to voice-transcribed prayers, the Elah and Glorify rings are reimagining traditional faith rituals for the wearable era.
body: Stressed? Heart rate elevated? If you’re wearing a smart ring from Oura, Ultrahuman, or Samsung, the spike could prompt app suggestions like breathing exercises, meditations, or a physical reset like a short walk. So far, so Silicon Valley. But now you can add reading the Bible to that list of self-soothing activities.

The first generation of Christian smart rings is here, joining other religious wearables like iQibla’s dedicated Muslim smartwatches, rings, and Hajj bands alongside “kosher” smartwatch apps. Two new devices in particular—Glorify’s Ring and Everblessed Technology’s Elah Ring—connect to hugely popular Christian prayer apps with tens of millions of users, and both claim to be the world’s first Christian smart ring.

Both are first, in their own ways. Everblessed’s $249 Elah Ring S1 went on sale in October and is shipping in the US. The $299 Glorify Ring launched in July, with reservations open and shipping set for January 2027, but 77,000 units of an earlier beta iteration, the Amen Ring made by faith tech company ConfideIn (which merged with Glorify this May), were given away last Christmas. Everblessed manages the Blessed app, and Glorify has an eponymous app.

highlights.title: How the Columbus Crew switched paths en route to the MLS playoffs
highlights.summary: In a transformative year, Crew GM Issa Tall’s boldest change may have been to abandon his best-laid plans. The Columbus Crew have a more holistic operation than most in MLS. The club as a whole still exists thanks to the dogged efforts of their fervent fanbase that helped block relocation.
body: And yet, this year tested the conventions set by team and league alike.

In January, chief soccer officer Issa Tall welcomed the club’s eighth head coach, Henrik Rydström. Having only previously coached in his native Sweden, the 50-year-old used his introductory presser to laud the values of relationism, to praise his predecessor, and to plot a bold course for a new Crew. It was assumed he’d be around a while – the Crew have historically been patient with coaches, needing only seven bosses to navigate their first 30 seasons.

By mid-May, after just 16 games in charge, Rydström was on his way back to Sweden. His five wins were the lowest of the eight full-time Crew coaches. And yet, Saturday sees the Crew begin the MLS Cup Playoffs in a best-of-three matchup with Lionel Messi and Inter Miami.

highlights.title: Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 3, Episodes 1 & 2 Recap and Review
highlights.summary: The first two episodes of Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 3 debut on Disney+ on Friday, November 20. The premiere of Percy Jackson Season 3 marks the first time an adaptation has made it past the second novel in Rick Riordan's series.
body: The first two episodes act as the setup for the main quest of Season 3. We get a proper introduction to Thalia as a key player, as well as new characters like Nico, Bianca, Artemis, Apollo, and Atlas. The premiere largely succeeds in its effort to kick off the story, and by the end of Episode 2 I found myself genuinely excited for more.

Walker Scobell has been a delightful Percy Jackson since Season 1, but he's only gotten better with experience. Whenever Percy is interacting with his friends or the gods themselves, all of the moving parts of the story seem to click in place. Tamara Smart also makes for a great Thalia, acting as the perfect counterbalance to Percy. These are two equally powerful demigods who are learning to deal with each other's existence, and the tension definitely comes through. The most engaging moments of the first two episodes are when the son of Poseidon and the daughter of Zeus find themselves at odds—which is pretty much constantly.

highlights.title: ‘I was drinking at 15, going to parties, being groomed and abused’: the grim reality of age-gap relationships
highlights.summary: Do teenagers need more protection from predatory adults? As campaigners in the UK call for changes to the law on consent, we talk to five people who became entangled with much older men and women.
body: I have spoken to people in their 40s, 50s, 60s and 70s, describing age gaps far greater than three years; often with people twice their age or more. It’s noticeable that social norms and taboos didn’t change hugely between the start of the 1960s and the end of the 80s; in most cases, their parents didn’t bat an eyelid and teachers, if they were aware, didn’t intervene. But the more striking through-line, from the 60s to the 00s, is how these relationships started – almost always through a position of power.

Liz, who is now 56, was an exception to that. When she was in her fifth year at school, she spent a lot of time with her brother, who was six years older. “I was drinking alcohol from the age of 15, going to parties with all these people,” she says. “Being groomed and abused, kind of … well, not kind of. I was groomed and abused, by more than one. This particular chap sticks out. He was by no means the worst person in my life, by the way.”

highlights.summary: Google is updating its homepage to include AI searches. In a post on X, Google's vice president of product, Robby Stein, shows how you can now open a collapsible sidebar to view and continue your AI chats.
body: You can now view your recent AI searches by opening the sidebar on Google’s homepage.

Based on the GIF shared by Stein, it looks like you can open the sidebar by clicking the gray bar that appears on the left side of your screen. From there, Google will show a list of the searches you’ve made using AI Mode, along with the ability to start a new thread, search your threads, or connect a Gemini Notebook.

It’s yet another big change for Google’s homepage, which has long presented you with a single bar to kick off your web search. The company brought its AI Mode button to its search bar last year, which opens up a chatbot-like search experience within Google. In May, Google updated its search box to accommodate longer queries and added AI-powered autocomplete.

Stein says Google is rolling out the option because “people are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done,” adding that “in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web.” The new homepage is rolling out globally on desktop.

highlights.title: AI is imposing a hidden ‘cognitive tax’ on the lowest-paid workers
highlights.summary: It’s time to rethink welfare as AI reshapes the economy and wears down the brains of some of the most vulnerable workers. AI is adding to the cognitive load of workers already stretched thin by unpredictable pay, insecure housing and mounting debt – and the lowest paid feel it most.
body: Throughout the history of the study of economics, the human brain, which directs our labour, judgment and resilience, has rarely been considered an asset in its own right. The emerging AI economy is changing that. As machines take on routine work, what becomes most valuable is the judgment, creativity and insights only people can provide. Economists coined a term for this in recent years: brain capital.
The World Economic Forum finds analytical thinking is now the skill employers value most, and estimates that 59 in every 100 workers will need training to adapt to this shift by 2030.

In September, I found myself at the first Global Brain Economy Summit in New York asking a hard question: How much room is there for creativity and learning when one’s mind is consumed by anxieties about paying rent or for food to last through the week?

body: Once again, Ubisoft used its financial update to praise the evergreen sales of its Assassin's Creed back catalog. Also, once again, it failed to provide any further detail on how last year's Assassin's Creed Shadows had fared. There's a sense that the long-awaited feudal Japan blockbuster has been a commercial disappointment for Ubisoft, and it's been a while since we had any formal update on sales numbers. No further content for the game is on the way, either — even though 2020's Valhalla just got a New Game Plus mode.

Indeed, Shadows is not mentioned at all in the results, despite Ubisoft commenting on Odyssey, Valhalla (which also just passed 40 million players), and this year's Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced — the latter of which has clearly had a successful launch.

Ubisoft attributes an outperformance in its latest financial results to Resynced, which it describes as having been "among the industry's most successful Action-Adventure remakes." How did its launch compare to any all-new Assassin's Creed games? If it did surpass any of those, Ubisoft perhaps understandably isn't saying — but it's clear the game has been a hit.

highlights.title: Experience: I discovered my dad was a killer on the run – and turned him in
highlights.summary: After a childhood marked by horrifying cruelty, the day finally came when I held my father’s life in the balance. Growing up, I lived in fear of my father’s moods. If there was too much ice in his drink or the sofa cushions weren’t lined up, he’d fly into a rage.
body: My parents managed apartments in the US, so we moved around a lot. I never got to make friends, so I assumed all fathers were the same.

I was eight when we went on a rare family holiday. Dad took me boating and could see I was nervous. “You need to face your fears,” he said, throwing me overboard. When I swam closer, he rowed away. By the time I made it to shore, I was exhausted.

When I was 16, we settled in Michigan. I started dating a girl called Lisa. I was worried about meeting her dad, but he was warm and welcoming. It was a revelation to discover not all men were angry and cruel.

I told Lisa how my father would hold my head under water and made me dangle from balconies. “Chip, that’s not OK,” she told me, horrified. I began to understand how abusive my childhood had been. I moved out, but couldn’t cut off my family completely.
points: After a childhood marked by horrifying cruelty, the day finally came when I held my father’s life in the balance.
Growing up, I lived in fear of my father’s moods.

body: We’ve already found Arthur Morgan’s hat in GTA 6, but there’s another thing connecting the two games. A readable book found in Brian’s Marina in Key Lento has multiple references to Red Dead Redemption and its sequel. X / Twitter user GameRoll shared excerpts from the book online. The book is a chronicle of the life and death of Flaco Hernandez, a gunslinger Arthur Morgan hunts to his cabin by Cairn Lake in Grizzlies West during the The Noblest of Men, and a Woman stranger mission in RDR 2. The book itself could even be the chronicle you help Theodore Levin write by hunting down the gunslingers, or at least a modern reinterpretation of it.

It’s told from the viewpoint of Rust McCreary, an original character who doesn’t appear in either RDR game. In the book, he comes across the corpse of Hernandez in the snow at Cairn Lake, right where you leave him in the RDR 2 mission.

According to the book, Hernandez had a bullet hole right in the center of his forehead, so it’s canon that you can actually aim good. The book also references multiple locations, from New Austin to Armadillo and Blackwater.
